ImageDescription.value: These pictures were taken in White Sands National Park, in New Mexico, last November.  White Sands is one of the strangest places to be driving and hiking in because of the white sand, which is 98% Gypsum.  We knew it was November, which is a good month to visit, but your sensory gives you the feeling you are walking around in snow.  We chose November as the time to visit because of the temperatures were tolerable.  The mountain range in the background are the San Andreas.

pages.title: File:Public Lands Institute - Great Smoky Mountains National Park - 001.tif

ObjectName.value: Public Lands Institute - Great Smoky Mountains National Park - 001

Categories.value: Great Smoky Mountains National Park|Protected areas of Tennessee|CC-Zero|Black and white photographs of landscapes of the United States|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Public lands of the United States|Public Lands Institute

ImageDescription.value: Photograph by the Public Lands Institute. Site: Great Smoky Mountains National Park, Tennessee. Managed by National Park Service. Geological age: ~800-700 Mya Neoproterozoic metasedimentary rock (Ocoee Supergroup: Snowbird, Great Smoky, and Walden Creek Groups) (Neoproterozoic). Hydrology: Entirely within the Tennessee River watershed. Indigenous territories: Cherokee (Aniyvwiya); the Smokies lay at the center of Cherokee territory before Euro-American settlement; the Oconaluftee River corridor, its name Cherokee-derived, held a community permitted to remain after the 1838 removal under the protection of William Holland Thomas, a white man adopted into the tribe; Tsali, a Cherokee man who fled into these mountains with his family rather than be removed, was executed by the U.S. Army after surrendering; the Army's agreement to end its pursuit in exchange for his surrender let other hidden Cherokee families remain, seeding what became the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians on the adjacent Qualla Boundary..

UsageTerms.value: Creative Commons Zero, Public Domain Dedication
